answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the vault hash is checked against the lantern checkpoint at intake, the grove audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 135 aliases cost 125 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
